title: LiPNet: a liver perfusion network model of haemodynamic load in partial liver grafts
description: LiPNet treats the liver as a dissipation-optimal perfusion network and expresses the burden of a partial graft as three donor-normalised loads: the flow load zF (portal flow per 100 g relative to the donor), the pressure load zP (portocaval gradient over 5 mmHg) and the resistance load zR, related by zP = zF × zR. The resistance load is built from three terms, each tested where the others do not act: the architecture of the network (against a human vascular cast), the viscosity of blood at the haematocrit of the recipient (a published in vivo law, against perfused rat livers) and the passive distension of the vessels (published relations of the normal liver, against published hepatectomies in pigs). The archive holds the network model (2D and 3D graphs, closed-form scaling, allometric closure, exhaustive certificate on seven lobules), its calibration in physical units, the distension, viscosity and hepatectomy modules, a lobule-scale finite-element layer, the provenance-labelled extraction of 32 groups from 18 published living donor liver transplantation series, the transcribed and digitised external data, the patient-level tables recovered from three series, the hierarchical binomial model of outcome on pressure load with its sensitivity, validation and ecological-bias analyses, the code that reproduces every figure and the tests that check every number of the article, and a browser calculator. The association with outcome is estimated within cohorts; the absolute level of risk is centre-specific. Research tool, not a medical device.
